description: This topic guides learners through applying the system and software development life cycle to plan, design, build, test, document and evaluate a practical computer studies project.

mcq.questionText: What is the FIRST stage when carrying out a software development project?
mcq.explanation: Every project begins by identifying and clearly defining the problem to be solved before any design or coding is done.

mcq.questionText: Which document states clearly what a project will and will not cover?
mcq.explanation: The scope defines the boundaries of a project, stating what is included and what is excluded to keep the work manageable.

mcq.questionText: A study done to check whether a proposed system is worth building in terms of cost, time and technology is called a:
mcq.explanation: A feasibility study assesses whether a project is practical and worthwhile in terms of cost, time, technology and operations.

mcq.questionText: Which fact-finding method involves asking respondents to fill in a printed set of written questions?
mcq.explanation: A questionnaire is a set of written questions distributed to respondents who fill in their answers, useful for collecting data from many people.

mcq.questionText: Which fact-finding method allows the analyst to watch how a task is actually performed at the workplace?
mcq.explanation: Observation means watching users carry out their tasks, which reveals what really happens rather than what people say happens.

mcq.questionText: During system design, deciding how data will be captured on screen forms is part of designing the:
mcq.explanation: Input design specifies how data enters the system, including the layout of data-entry screens and forms.

mcq.questionText: Which type of test data is deliberately wrong or outside the accepted format to check whether the system rejects it?
mcq.explanation: Abnormal or invalid data is incorrect data used to confirm the program detects and rejects errors instead of accepting them.

mcq.questionText: If a field accepts marks from 0 to 100, testing with the values 0 and 100 is an example of using:
mcq.explanation: Boundary or extreme data lies at the edges of the acceptable range, such as 0 and 100, to check the limits are handled correctly.

mcq.questionText: Testing a single module or program on its own before combining it with others is called:
mcq.explanation: Unit testing checks each individual module or component separately, while system testing checks the complete integrated system.

mcq.questionText: Which changeover method switches off the old system completely and starts the new one immediately?
mcq.explanation: Direct (immediate) changeover stops the old system at once and replaces it with the new system, which is cheap but risky.

mcq.questionText: Running the old and new systems together at the same time for a period to compare results is called:
mcq.explanation: In parallel changeover both systems operate together so results can be compared, giving safety but at a higher cost.

mcq.questionText: Introducing a new system in only one branch or department first before spreading it elsewhere is called:
mcq.explanation: Pilot changeover installs the new system in one part of the organisation first; if successful it is then rolled out to the rest.

mcq.questionText: A step-by-step guide written to help ordinary end users operate the new system is known as:
mcq.explanation: User documentation (the user manual) explains in simple terms how to use the system, while technical documentation targets programmers and maintainers.

mcq.questionText: Correcting errors and improving a system after it has been put into use is part of which stage?
mcq.explanation: Maintenance is the ongoing activity of fixing faults and improving the system after implementation to keep it useful.

mcq.questionText: A chart that shows project tasks against time so that scheduling and progress can be tracked is called a:
mcq.explanation: A Gantt chart is a bar chart that lists tasks against a timeline, helping teams plan, schedule and monitor a project.

fib.questionText: The overall process of planning, building and maintaining a system through defined stages is called the system development _____ cycle.
fib.explanation: The System Development Life Cycle (SDLC) is the framework of stages followed when developing a system.

fib.questionText: A clear statement of what a project intends to achieve is known as its _____.
fib.explanation: Objectives state exactly what the project should accomplish and act as criteria for judging its success.

fib.questionText: A face-to-face conversation in which an analyst asks a user spoken questions to gather facts is called an _____.
fib.explanation: An interview is a direct question-and-answer session that allows detailed information and follow-up questions.

fib.questionText: Designing how processed results will be presented to users, for example as reports or screens, is called _____ design.
fib.explanation: Output design determines how the results produced by the system are displayed or printed for the user.

fib.questionText: The stage in which the actual program statements are written using a programming language is called _____.
fib.explanation: Coding (programming) is where the design is turned into working program instructions written in a chosen language.

fib.questionText: Test data that is correct and within the expected range used to check normal operation is called _____ data.
fib.explanation: Normal (valid) data is acceptable data within the expected range, used to confirm the system works under typical conditions.

fib.questionText: Testing the whole finished system to confirm all parts work together is called _____ testing.
fib.explanation: System testing checks the complete integrated system to ensure all modules function correctly together.

fib.questionText: Introducing a new system one part or module at a time is known as _____ changeover.
fib.explanation: In phased changeover the new system is introduced gradually, one stage or section at a time.

fib.questionText: Documentation written for programmers, showing code, flowcharts and file structures, is called _____ documentation.
fib.explanation: Technical documentation describes the internal workings of the system to help programmers maintain and modify it.

fib.questionText: Sharing tasks among members and cooperating to complete a project on time is an example of _____.
fib.explanation: Teamwork involves members cooperating and sharing responsibilities so the project is completed efficiently.

tf.questionText: A feasibility study is carried out to decide whether a proposed project is worth doing before resources are committed.
tf.explanation: The feasibility study determines if the project is practical and worthwhile before full development begins.

tf.questionText: The problem definition stage should be done only after the program has been fully coded.
tf.explanation: The problem must be identified and defined at the very start, long before any coding takes place.

tf.questionText: Interviews, questionnaires, observation and document study are all valid fact-finding methods.
tf.explanation: These four are the common fact-finding techniques used to gather requirements about an existing situation.

tf.questionText: Boundary (extreme) test data is used to check how the system behaves at the edges of the acceptable range.
tf.explanation: Boundary data tests the limits of the valid range to ensure values at the edges are handled correctly.

tf.questionText: Direct changeover is the safest method because the old system continues running as a backup.
tf.explanation: Direct changeover is the riskiest method because the old system is switched off immediately with no backup; parallel running is the safest.

tf.questionText: Unit testing checks individual modules, while system testing checks the complete integrated system.
tf.explanation: Unit testing focuses on single components and system testing verifies the whole system working together.

tf.questionText: User documentation is intended mainly for programmers who will modify the source code.
tf.explanation: User documentation is for end users; technical documentation is the one intended for programmers.

tf.questionText: Maintenance of a system stops completely once the system has been implemented.
tf.explanation: Maintenance continues after implementation to correct errors and improve the system over its lifetime.

tf.questionText: A Gantt chart can be used to schedule project tasks and monitor progress over time.
tf.explanation: A Gantt chart maps tasks against a timeline, making it useful for scheduling and tracking project progress.

tf.questionText: Defining the scope of a project helps to prevent the work from growing beyond what was planned.
tf.explanation: A clearly defined scope sets boundaries and helps avoid uncontrolled expansion of the project work.

summary.questionText: Name any one stage of the system development life cycle.
summary.correctAnswer: Problem identification (or feasibility study, requirements gathering, design, coding, testing, implementation, maintenance)
summary.explanation: The SDLC stages include problem identification, feasibility, requirements gathering, design, coding, testing, implementation and maintenance.

summary.questionText: State one purpose of a feasibility study in a software project.
summary.correctAnswer: To determine whether the project is worth doing in terms of cost, time and technology
summary.explanation: The feasibility study checks if the project is practical and worthwhile before full commitment of resources.

summary.questionText: List the four common fact-finding methods used in requirements gathering.
summary.correctAnswer: Interviews, questionnaires, observation and document analysis
summary.explanation: These four techniques are used to collect information about the existing system and user needs.

summary.questionText: Name the five main areas considered during system design.
summary.correctAnswer: Input, processing, output, files/database and user interface
summary.explanation: System design covers how data is entered, processed, output, stored, and how users interact with the system.

summary.questionText: Identify the three categories of test data used when testing a program.
summary.correctAnswer: Normal data, boundary (extreme) data and abnormal (invalid) data
summary.explanation: Programs are tested with normal, boundary and abnormal data to confirm correct handling of all cases.

summary.questionText: List the four methods of system changeover.
summary.correctAnswer: Direct, parallel, phased and pilot changeover
summary.explanation: These are the four ways of switching from an old system to a new one during implementation.

summary.questionText: Differentiate between user documentation and technical documentation.
summary.correctAnswer: User documentation guides end users on how to operate the system, while technical documentation helps programmers understand and maintain the code
summary.explanation: User documentation targets operators; technical documentation targets developers and maintainers.

summary.questionText: State one reason why maintenance is important after a system is implemented.
summary.correctAnswer: To correct errors and improve the system so it continues to meet user needs
summary.explanation: Maintenance keeps the system reliable and up to date by fixing faults and making improvements.

summary.questionText: Mention one tool used for planning and scheduling project tasks.
summary.explanation: A Gantt chart shows tasks against time and helps schedule and monitor a project.

summary.questionText: State one benefit of teamwork when carrying out a software development project.
summary.correctAnswer: Tasks are shared so the project is completed faster and more efficiently
summary.explanation: Teamwork allows division of labour and cooperation, leading to quicker and better results.

hoq.questionText: A school wants to record students' termly marks. The data-entry field for a subject mark accepts whole numbers from 0 to 100. Which set of test data BEST checks the boundary (extreme) cases of this field?
hoq.explanation: Boundary data uses the values at the edges of the valid range. For 0 to 100, the boundary values are 0 and 100, while -5/150 are abnormal and 45/60 are normal.

hoq.questionText: A hospital is replacing its patient records system. The data is critical and any loss could endanger lives, but the budget is large. Which changeover method is MOST suitable?
hoq.explanation: Parallel changeover runs both systems together so results can be compared and no data is lost, making it safest for critical data when budget allows.

hoq.questionText: A student team finished coding a library system but skipped writing any documentation. Six months later a new member cannot understand how the code works. Which stage was poorly done and what is the consequence?

options.text: Feasibility study; the project became too expensive
Requirements gathering; the wrong system was built
Documentation; maintenance becomes difficult because the code is hard to understand
Testing; the system has no errors at all

hoq.explanation: Without technical documentation, future programmers struggle to understand the code, making maintenance slow and error-prone.
